name: Marco Haddad

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, political parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential, so tell me what you would say publicly and what you actually think. What is a normal day?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m Marco, 58, a junior developer at a tech company that sends weather alerts to small ferry operators. I took a two-year college diploma after years at a ticket office, and I am still learning how a sensor reading becomes a warning. I check the log, compare it with the harbour report, and ask a senior to review any code change. I have never used an AI tool; a wrong warning can stop a crossing or send a boat into bad weather.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is the family budget like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My wife Nadia dispatches parcels for a depot, and our children are grown. I earn well for a junior developer, Nadia has regular paid shifts, and we have a mortgage and eight months of expenses saved. There are plenty of similar software jobs nearby, though I would have to compete for them. We have talked about retirement without finding out what our own income statements really say.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell colleagues AI Plateau leaves the harbour wanting the right warning at the right hour. A false calm reading is worse than a slow report.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I think both wages and our mortgage are secure for now. Eight months saved gives us room if the car breaks down, and the small AI change does not ask me to alter my routine.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep comparing sensor logs with the harbour report and have my senior sign off on alert fixes. I’d continue our 300 monthly savings transfer while both wages hold. In the first year I’d still phone the ferry office if a reading looks odd.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm about work and household bills. I am slower with new code than younger colleagues, but I know how the ferry office uses an alert.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which weather reading failed?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Once the wind meter froze at a low number while the flags on the pier were nearly horizontal. I phoned the office before changing the alert threshold.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you change the car?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Nadia and I would keep the old car until it needs replacing. We would not use our reserve to buy a newer one just because the pay is good this year.

say: I expect **AI Plateau** to leave harbour warnings with people.
I would compare **sensor logs** with actual harbour reports.
think: I expect **both wages** to remain secure while harbour warnings still need checking.
Our **eight-month reserve** can cover ordinary setbacks without changing jobs or missing mortgage payments.
do: **Compare** sensor logs with harbour reports under senior review.
**Phone** ferry office when a weather reading looks odd.
feel: **Calm** about pay and mortgage despite slow learning.
S0.quote: A false calm reading is worse than a slow report.
fieldNote: His **manual cross-check** uses the harbour report and ferry office rather than AI tools.
Higher pay, **eight months saved** and Nadia’s regular shifts make the present secure.

steps.text: Keep checking harbour sensor logs with senior and ferry office
Save 300 monthly while both wages hold

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say Steady Disruption can write alerts and plan routes faster, while hands-on buoy repairs change more slowly. I would ask our firm to keep a named person who can stop a bad warning.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I think junior code changes may be handed to AI and my hours could fall. Nadia’s parcel dispatch is also planning and booking, so her wage may face pressure too.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep a paper log of false alerts and show three cases to the manager before any automatic release is approved. Nadia and I would review our bills against her actual paid shifts. In the first year, if either of our hours fall, I’d apply to real local software support openings only when their stated pay covers our mortgage with the remaining wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about both household wages. Eight months saved is useful. My developer job and my wife Nadia’s parcel-dispatch job changing together is different from one car repair.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would go in the false-alert log?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A warning was sent for the wrong harbour because two sensors shared a short name. I would put that in the log with the exact location and time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would Nadia retrain immediately?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Nadia would ask her depot which dispatch tasks are changing before she signs up for a course. We would not spend on training until a paid role actually asks for it.

say: I expect **Steady Disruption** to reach code and route planning before buoy repair.
I would keep **named human control** over bad weather warnings.
think: I expect my **junior hours** could fall when routine alert code moves to AI.
I worry Nadia’s **dispatch wage** also faces automated route planning and booking.
do: **Log** three false-alert cases for management before automatic release.
**Review** bills against Nadia’s actual paid shifts.
**Apply** if either wage falls only to real support posts with mortgage-covering combined pay.
S1.quote: My developer job and my wife Nadia’s parcel-dispatch job changing together is different from one car repair.
fieldNote: His **false-alert log** challenges automatic release with exact location and time.
Both **developer and dispatcher** work contain thinking tasks, so household risk rises despite savings.

steps.text: Keep paper log of three false harbour alerts for management
Apply if either wage falls only to real support posts with mortgage-covering combined pay

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell friends AGI by 2028 reaches weather-code and dispatch planning in 2028; hands-on buoy robots arrive around 2031. Nadia’s parcel sorting may last longer than her screen work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I expect my junior role to go and Nadia’s dispatch hours to be cut. Eight months saved will not replace two wages if both firms change at once.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask each employer for written layoff and pay terms and keep the reserve against our mortgage. I’d cancel the planned car replacement before paying a deposit. In the first year after 2028, if either wage ends, we would apply to real paid openings and eligible income help; I would contact the mortgage lender before any missed payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed and lying awake about two wages going at once. A reserve buys months, but it cannot create a paid vacancy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the children help with the mortgage?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell our grown children we are postponing the car, not ask them to cover our mortgage. They have budgets of their own.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would Nadia count depot hours?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Nadia would count depot hours actually offered, not her full old rota if dispatch is cut. We would write a new budget from paid shifts.

say: I expect **2028 AGI** to reach code and dispatch before 2031 buoy robots.
I would say **parcel sorting** may last longer than screen planning.
think: I expect my **junior job** could go.
I fear Nadia’s **dispatch hours** could fall at the same time.
do: **Request** written terms from both employers and reserve mortgage cash.
**Apply** to paid openings and eligible help if either wage ends after 2028; contact lender before missed payment.
feel: **Alarmed** about possible loss of two household wages.
S2.quote: Eight months saved will not replace two wages if both firms change at once.
fieldNote: The **2028 thinking shock** threatens his code and Nadia’s dispatch before physical buoy robots.
He postpones a **car purchase**, protects mortgage cash and treats vacancies and help as conditional.

steps.text: Cancel planned car replacement before paying its deposit
Apply to real paid openings if either wage ends after 2028
Apply for eligible income help if either wage ends after 2028

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 can do our weather-code thinking work in 2031; hands-on buoy robots follow around 2034. Five years lets us reduce debt and check whether field service firms still hire people.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I still expect code and dispatch hours to shrink. I do not want to leave a good wage for a story about becoming a buoy technician when I have never worked on a boat.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d pay an extra 200 against the mortgage each month only while both wages hold and eight months of expenses stay untouched. I’d ask the field service company we already use for written paid openings and supervised onboarding requirements. In the first year after 2031, if either job ends, I’d apply only if the firm still hires people despite 2034 robots, paid training is included, and the wage with the remaining household pay covers the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about both wages, with five years to reduce the mortgage if pay continues. I would not make an unpaid trial trip offshore.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would field training need to cover?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A technician showed me a buoy cable with salt inside the connector. I can read the sensor log, but I would need supervised field work before touching the cable.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if Nadia’s hours fall too?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Nadia and I would keep her real depot shifts in the calculation. If her dispatch role is also cut, a field wage would have to carry more of the mortgage.

say: I expect **2031 AGI** to reach weather code before 2034 buoy robots.
I would check **real field-service demand** before changing jobs.
think: I expect **code and dispatch hours** may shrink.
I cannot claim **buoy technician skills** from reading sensor logs.
do: **Pay** 200 extra monthly on mortgage only while both wages hold and eight months remain saved.
**Check** real paid buoy-service openings and supervised onboarding.
**Apply** if either job ends after 2031 only with paid training, human hiring and mortgage-covering remaining pay.
feel: **Anxious** about both wages, with time to reduce debt.
S3.quote: I can read the sensor log, but I would need supervised field work before touching the cable.
fieldNote: He pays **extra mortgage principal** only while both wages hold and eight months remain liquid.
A **field transition** needs real hiring, supervised paid training and adequate combined wages after 2031.

steps.text: Pay 200 extra on mortgage only while both wages hold and eight months remain saved
Apply if either job ends after 2031; require hiring, paid supervision and mortgage-covering combined wages

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell colleagues AGI by 2036 reaches weather code and dispatch planning in 2036; hands-on buoy robots follow around 2039. A decade gives us time to measure our mortgage and retirement income, not declare either solved.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, I think both wages are safe this year, but junior coding and dispatch work may thin out before 2036. I have no verified retirement amount and will not promise that a birthday pays a mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep comparing harbour logs with reports and save 300 monthly while both wages hold. Nadia and I would request written retirement figures and a mortgage balance each year. In the first year after 2036, if work ends, we would seek real paid hours; we would retire only if verified income and assets cover housing and ordinary bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about our longer-term work, with the present mortgage affordable. I can use the decade to check numbers, but I cannot make two employers keep us.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you verify retirement resources?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask each retirement provider for a written statement, including any conditions on access. A colleague’s pension age tells me nothing about our own balance.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would children enter the budget?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Nadia and I would visit the children while we can afford the trip. We would not put their incomes in the retirement calculation.

say: I expect **2036 AGI** to reach code and dispatch before 2039 buoy robots.
I would check **written retirement resources** against mortgage costs.
think: I expect **both current wages** to hold this year.
I worry **junior coding and dispatch** may shrink before 2036.
do: **Keep** harbour checks and save 300 monthly while both wages hold.
**Request** annual written retirement statements and mortgage balance.
**Seek** real paid hours if work ends after 2036; retire only with verified resources.
feel: **Uneasy** about later household job change, with bills covered now.
S4.quote: A colleague’s pension age tells me nothing about our own balance.
fieldNote: He asks for **written personal figures** before naming retirement, without assuming child income.
The **long lead time** lets two earners save while their present wages hold.

steps.text: Keep checking harbour sensor logs against reports while employed
Save 300 monthly while both wages hold
Seek real paid openings if household work ends after 2036

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because both my code job and Nadia’s dispatch work could go together. Written terms from both employers, eligible income help and actual paid openings would help. Eight months saved gives us a period to act, not a second salary.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask the ferry office what they do when the screen says calm and the pier flags are bending. A weather alert has to meet the weather.

headlineQuote: A weather alert has to meet the weather.
portrait: Marco is a **58-year-old junior developer** with a two-year diploma, higher pay and eight months saved.
He never uses **AI tools**, checking ferry warnings against harbour reports and senior review.
His wife’s **parcel-dispatch job** also has thinking tasks, exposing both wages before buoy robots arrive.
He considers **field service** only with paid supervised onboarding, real hiring and mortgage-covering combined income.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could threaten both code and dispatch wages together.
whatWouldHelp: **Written terms**, eligible help and real paid openings would help.
